subject: OBG
title: Postpartum Hemorrhage: Recognition and Emergency Response
preview: Rapidly identify excessive postpartum bleeding, resuscitate and address uterine tone, tissue, trauma and coagulation.

sections.title: Recognize maternal shock
points: Blood loss may be underestimated visually, and vital signs may lag; assess cumulative loss and perfusion.
Activate emergency support early when bleeding persists or maternal physiology worsens.

sections.title: Act on the cause
points: Assess uterine tone and genital tract trauma while coordinating blood products and definitive interventions when necessary.
Current evidence-based PPH bundles and local protocols guide dose, route and sequencing.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: The four Ts of postpartum hemorrhage: Tone, Tissue, Trauma and Thrombin.
A firm uterus makes alternative sources such as trauma, tissue and coagulation particularly important to assess.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A firm uterus with ongoing bleeding should prompt attention to trauma, retained tissue and coagulation causes.
Do not delay escalation while waiting for an arbitrary blood-loss number.

quickRevision: The four Ts—Tone, Tissue, Trauma and Thrombin—provide a practical framework for causes of postpartum hemorrhage.
Uterine atony is common, but lacerations, retained tissue and coagulopathy need active assessment.
A coordinated response combines uterine measures, uterotonics, resuscitation and appropriate escalation.

quiz.question: What is a major immediate treatment component for uterine atony causing PPH?
quiz.explanation: Uterine massage and appropriate uterotonics. Assess uterine tone and genital tract trauma while coordinating blood products and definitive interventions when necessary.
